question: The cost price of a laptop is ₹78,200. If the loss percentage is 44%, then what is the selling price (in ₹) of the laptop?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Loss = 44% = 44 ÷ 100 = 11 ÷ 25

Cost Price (CP) = 25 units, Loss = 11 units

Selling Price (SP) = CP − Loss = 25 − 11 = 14 units

25 units = 78200 ⇒ 1 unit = 78200 ÷ 25 = 3128

Selling Price (14 units) = 14 × 3128 = 43792

**∴ The correct answer is ₹43,792.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) of the laptop = ₹78,200

Loss Percentage = 44%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × [ (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100 ]

 
 Cost Price = 100% (₹78,200)

 
 SP = 56%

 
 Loss = 44%

 

 

 

 
 SP = 100% − 44% = 56% of CP

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 78200 × [ (100 − 44) ÷ 100 ]

⇒ SP = 78200 × (56 ÷ 100)

⇒ SP = 78200 × 0.56

⇒ SP = 782 × 56

⇒ SP = 43792

**∴ The correct answer is ₹43,792.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basic Formulas

Profit = SP − CP | Loss = CP − SP.

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 | Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100. Always remember that both profit and loss percentages are calculated on the Cost Price by default.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always offered on the Marked Price (MP). To find the selling price after a discount: SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.
